title: We fought for the royal Stuarts that reneged us against the Williamites and they betrayed us.
html_source:
The Williamite War in Ireland (in Irish, Cogadh an Dá Rí, meaning “War of the Two Kings”) took place from 1688–1691. In 1688, during the Glorious Revolution, Stuart King James II was deposed by Dutch Protestant Prince William of Orange, James' own nephew and son-in-law, amid growing fears about James' Catholicism, his ties to France, and the birth of a son who would interrupted the expected succession of his Protestant daughter Mary (wife of William and later Queen, co-regnant with William) to the throne.

James was supported by the mostly Catholic Ireland (supporters of the Stuart dynasty were known as “Jacobites”, cf. “James”) and tried to use the country as a base to regain his kingship. However, Protestants in the north of the country (“Williamites”) supported an invasion by William and forces from several other nations (including Dutch and Danish troops). In the ensuing wars in Ireland, James was outmanned; the turning point was at the Battle of the Boyne (1690) which saw many Jacobite losses, after which James fled the Island. The war had a lasting impact on Ireland, confirming British (and Protestant) rule over the island that would last for more than 200 years.
